questions.prompt: Of what two parts do most Kinyarwanda words consist?
questions.answer: A prefix and a root or stem

questions.prompt: What part of speech determines the forms of all the other words in the sentence that are dependent on it?
questions.answer: The noun

questions.prompt: What distinguishes one class of nouns from another?
questions.answer: The prefixes

questions.prompt: What are the class prefixes, singular, and plural, for the class that deals exclusively with people?
questions.answer: Umu- and aba-

questions.prompt: Are any "people" nouns contained in any other class? If so which?
questions.answer: Class 3

questions.prompt: If you suppose a noun beginning with umu- is not a personal noun, into which class would you put it?
questions.answer: Class 2

questions.prompt: What are the demonstrative adjectives that go with umu- and aba-? With imi-? With -in?
questions.answer: Uyu, uriya, aba, barajya; uyu, uriya, iyi, iriya; iyi, iriya, izi, ziriya

questions.prompt: What's wrong with Aragenda i Butare? How should it be said? How about umuhungu mubi? Ndajya mw inzu?
questions.answer: You can't use -genda with a place concept following it. Arajya i Butare. A demonstrative adjective removes the initial vowel from the noun that follows it: mu nzu

questions.prompt: When is the vowel of ni, si, and na omitted?
questions.answer: When it is followed by a vowel

questions.prompt: List the possessive adjectives for class 2 (wanjye, etc)
questions.answer: Wanjye, wawe, we; wacu, wanyu, wabo; yanjye, yawe, ywe; yacu, yanyu, yabo

questions.prompt: What happens to r when it follows n? Give a few examples
questions.answer: It becomes d. n-ri becomes n-di; n-re-n-re becomes n-d-en-de, n-rabizi becomes n-dabizi

questions.prompt: When a noun is qualified by an adjective and a possessive pronoun, what is the correct order?
questions.answer: Noun possessive pronoun, adjective, as in ibintu byacu nyinshi
